curation.notes: Difficulty is a practical study judgment, not a claim about which words the learner personally knows.

notes: Attach these article contexts to existing canonical IDs; do not replace their lexical fields or use the literary chapter importer.

items.meaning: 协作过载；团队协作需求超出可用时间和精力
items.definitionEn: A situation in which demands for collaboration exceed the time and energy people can reasonably provide.
items.usage: 本文核心概念；问题在于需求过多或分配不均，并不表示合作本身没有价值。
items.exampleEn: We reduced collaborative overload by routing routine questions to a shared knowledge base.
items.exampleZh: 我们把常见问题转交到共享知识库处理，从而减轻了协作过载。

items.meaning: 削弱生产力；逐渐消耗工作效率
items.definitionEn: To gradually reduce the amount or quality of useful work people can produce.
items.usage: sap 作动词表示削弱、消耗；语境强调过量协作对效率的影响。
items.exampleEn: Repeated status calls can sap productivity when no decisions are needed.
items.exampleZh: 如果没有需要作出的决定，反复召开进度电话会议可能削弱工作效率。

items.meaning: 跨职能的；涉及不同业务部门的
items.definitionEn: Involving people or work from different functions or departments in an organization.
items.usage: 与 interdisciplinary 跨学科不同，通常强调销售、运营、技术等职能之间的合作。
items.exampleEn: A cross-functional group reviewed how the pricing change would affect customers.
items.exampleZh: 一个跨职能小组审查了价格调整将如何影响客户。

items.meaning: 组织中的信息孤岛；各自为政的部门
items.definitionEn: A part of an organization that works separately and shares too little information with others.
items.usage: 本文为组织管理比喻，不是储粮筒仓；常见 break down silos。
items.exampleEn: Shared project goals helped the departments move beyond their silos.
items.exampleZh: 共同的项目目标帮助各部门走出了各自为政的状态。

items.meaning: （壁垒或隔阂）逐步瓦解；消除或削弱壁垒
items.definitionEn: For a barrier or organizational separation to disappear or weaken, or to cause it to do so.
items.usage: 本文 silos are breaking down 指部门壁垒逐步瓦解；也可及物：break down barriers。区分计划或安排失败的另一义项。
items.exampleEn: Joint customer interviews helped break down barriers between design and support.
items.exampleZh: 共同开展客户访谈帮助消除了设计与客服之间的壁垒。

items.meaning: 急剧增加；迅速膨胀
items.definitionEn: To increase rapidly and become much larger.
items.usage: 本文指协作活动所占时间增长；动词用法常见于成本、预算或工作量。
items.exampleEn: The review process ballooned as more teams requested a separate meeting.
items.exampleZh: 随着越来越多团队要求单独开会，审查流程迅速膨胀。

items.meaning: 突然大幅上升；激增
items.definitionEn: To rise sharply over a short period of time.
items.usage: 本文指资源消耗突然增加；区别于稳定、缓慢的上升。
items.exampleEn: Requests for technical support spiked after the new platform launched.
items.exampleZh: 新平台上线后，技术支持请求激增。

items.meaning: 使某人停下来认真考虑；引起顾虑
items.definitionEn: To make someone hesitate or reconsider because something raises a concern.
items.usage: pause 在此不是简单暂停活动，而是因发现问题而重新思考。
items.exampleEn: The number of unresolved complaints gave the launch committee pause.
items.exampleZh: 尚未解决的投诉数量让发布委员会产生了顾虑。

items.meaning: 在某个数值附近徘徊；大致保持在
items.definitionEn: To remain close to a particular level or amount.
items.usage: 用于比例、成本等数值；不表示精确等于所给数字。
items.exampleEn: Meeting attendance hovered around seventy percent throughout the pilot.
items.exampleZh: 试点期间，会议出席率一直在百分之七十左右徘徊。

items.meaning: 大量涌来的请求；使人应接不暇的请求
items.definitionEn: A very large number of requests arriving in a way that is difficult to manage.
items.usage: 原文 avalanche of requests 跨行；avalanche 在此为雪崩式涌入的比喻。
items.exampleEn: The policy change triggered an avalanche of requests for clarification.
items.exampleZh: 政策调整引发了大量要求解释的请求。

items.meaning: 职业倦怠；长期工作压力导致的身心耗竭
items.definitionEn: A state of physical or emotional exhaustion associated with prolonged work-related stress.
items.usage: 此义通常不可数；不把一时疲惫直接等同于 burnout。
items.exampleEn: The department reviewed workloads after several employees raised concerns about burnout.
items.exampleZh: 几名员工表达了对职业倦怠的担忧后，部门重新审视了工作量。

items.meaning: 员工流失；人员离职与更替
items.definitionEn: The rate or process at which employees leave an organization and are replaced.
items.usage: 本文为人员流失义，不是营业额或库存周转率；通常不可数。
items.exampleEn: The manager examined whether frequent weekend requests were increasing turnover.
items.exampleZh: 经理调查了频繁的周末工作请求是否正在增加员工流失。

items.meaning: 严重失衡的；分配明显不均的
items.definitionEn: Unevenly balanced, with too much concentrated on one side or in one group.
items.usage: 本文指少数员工承担过多协作工作，而非物体外形歪斜。
items.exampleEn: The workload became lopsided when every urgent request went to the same analyst.
items.exampleZh: 当每个紧急请求都交给同一位分析师时，工作量分配变得严重失衡。

items.meaning: 增值的；带来实际额外价值的
items.definitionEn: Producing an additional useful benefit beyond what was already available.
items.usage: 本文修饰有效协作或活动；不是仅增加活动数量，也不是增值税。
items.exampleEn: We shortened routine updates to protect time for value-added analysis.
items.exampleZh: 我们缩短了常规汇报，以保留时间开展能带来额外价值的分析。

items.meaning: 额外付出者；经常超出本职要求作贡献的员工
items.definitionEn: An employee who regularly contributes beyond the formal requirements of their role.
items.usage: 这是文章引用的人员标签；常见相关表达 go the extra mile，不把该标签当作正式职位名称。
items.exampleEn: The team valued its extra milers but checked that their help did not become an unlimited obligation.
items.exampleZh: 团队重视愿意额外付出的成员，也检查他们的帮助是否变成了没有边界的义务。
collocations: an extra miler on the team

items.meaning: 良性循环；有利因素相互强化的过程
items.definitionEn: A process in which positive effects reinforce one another and create further benefits.
items.usage: cycle 强调反馈循环；与 vicious cycle 恶性循环相对，原文随后说循环可能变坏。
items.exampleEn: Reliable documentation created a virtuous cycle of fewer interruptions and better updates.
items.exampleZh: 可靠的文档形成了打扰更少、更新更完善的良性循环。

items.meaning: 瓶颈；限制整体进展的环节或人员
items.definitionEn: A point in a process where limited capacity slows the progress of the whole system.
items.usage: 本文指工作必须等少数关键协作者处理后才能推进。
items.exampleEn: A single approval inbox became a bottleneck during the hiring surge.
items.exampleZh: 在集中招聘期间，唯一的审批收件箱成了流程瓶颈。

items.meaning: 发表意见；介入讨论提供判断
items.definitionEn: To contribute an opinion or judgment to a discussion or decision.
items.usage: 常用 weigh in on an issue；不是称重，也不同于 weigh up 评估。
items.exampleEn: We asked the compliance specialist to weigh in before finalizing the contract.
items.exampleZh: 在敲定合同前，我们请合规专家发表意见。

items.meaning: 负担过重的；被过度消耗的
items.definitionEn: Required to do more work or provide more effort than one can reasonably manage.
items.usage: 本文指人的时间和精力受到过度索取，不是税率过高。
items.exampleEn: The overtaxed coordinator could no longer respond to every department promptly.
items.exampleZh: 这位负担过重的协调员已无法及时回复每个部门。

items.meaning: 获得回报；享受努力带来的成果
items.definitionEn: To receive the benefits produced by an effort, investment, or action.
items.usage: 常接 of；原义 reap 为收割，商业语境中为获得成果。
items.exampleEn: Teams can reap the rewards of shared templates long after the first project ends.
items.exampleZh: 第一个项目结束很久以后，团队仍能从共享模板中获得回报。

items.meaning: 无意地；不经意间
items.definitionEn: Without intending to do something or realizing its consequences.
items.usage: 表示行为或结果不是有意造成，不等于结果没有责任或影响。
items.exampleEn: The new approval rule inadvertently increased the manager's workload.
items.exampleZh: 新的审批规定无意中增加了经理的工作量。

items.meaning: 耗尽；大幅消耗资源
items.definitionEn: To use up or greatly reduce an available supply of something.
items.usage: 可接时间、精力或库存；本文对照说明共享知识通常不会耗掉持有者的知识。
items.exampleEn: Constant interruptions depleted the analyst's energy before her main task began.
items.exampleZh: 在主要任务开始前，持续的打扰就大量消耗了分析师的精力。

items.meaning: 资料库；集中保存信息的地方
items.definitionEn: A place or system where information or materials are stored for later use.
items.usage: 本文包括报告和知识库；不只指软件代码仓库。
items.exampleEn: We created a searchable repository of answers to recurring customer questions.
items.exampleZh: 我们建立了一个可搜索的资料库，收录反复出现的客户问题的答案。

items.meaning: 通过激励促使某人采取行动
items.definitionEn: To encourage a behavior by offering rewards or other benefits.
items.usage: 常用 incentivize someone to do something；激励是否奏效取决于奖励与目标是否一致。
items.exampleEn: The bonus plan should incentivize accurate handovers rather than rushed closures.
items.exampleZh: 奖金计划应激励准确交接，而不是匆忙结案。

items.meaning: 使承受过大压力；使资源紧张
items.definitionEn: To place heavy demands on a person's or system's available capacity.
items.usage: 本文指过长的协作活动加重双方时间精力负担；不是肌肉拉伤义。
items.exampleEn: Repeated urgent changes strained the small team's capacity.
items.exampleZh: 反复出现的紧急变更加重了小团队的负担。

items.meaning: 声誉卓著且实力雄厚的
items.definitionEn: Established, financially strong, and widely respected.
items.usage: 本文修饰专业服务公司；并非字面上的蓝色芯片。
items.exampleEn: She joined a blue-chip consulting firm with a large international client base.
items.exampleZh: 她加入了一家声誉卓著、拥有大量国际客户的咨询公司。

items.meaning: 阻碍；妨碍进展或表现
items.definitionEn: To make an activity, process, or person's progress more difficult.
items.usage: 不一定完全阻止；可指拖慢或降低表现。
items.exampleEn: Unclear ownership can hinder the team's ability to solve urgent problems.
items.exampleZh: 责任归属不清会妨碍团队解决紧急问题。

items.meaning: 主动离职；员工自愿离开的流失
items.definitionEn: Employee departures that occur because employees choose to leave.
items.usage: 区别于裁员或解雇导致的非自愿离职；此语义通常不可数。
items.exampleEn: The firm interviewed departing staff to understand the rise in voluntary turnover.
items.exampleZh: 公司访谈了离职员工，以了解主动离职增加的原因。

items.meaning: 好心反招麻烦；善举有时会带来额外负担
items.definitionEn: An ironic saying that helping others can sometimes lead to trouble or unwanted consequences.
items.usage: 常见讽刺性谚语，表示善举有时反而带来麻烦；本文借此描述助人者被更多请求压垮，并非作者原创句或鼓励拒绝帮助。
items.exampleEn: After her helpful checklist led to twenty new requests, she joked that no good deed goes unpunished.
items.exampleZh: 她提供的实用清单引来了二十个新请求后，她打趣说真是好心反招麻烦。
collocations: feel that no good deed goes unpunished
joke that no good deed goes unpunished

items.meaning: 缺乏投入感的；对工作疏离的
items.definitionEn: No longer mentally or emotionally involved in one's work.
items.usage: 本文指工作投入感低，不等于没有被安排工作；甚至可能同时工作过载。
items.exampleEn: The employee appeared disengaged after months of unrecognized support work.
items.exampleZh: 连续几个月的支持工作未获认可后，这名员工显得对工作缺乏投入感。

items.meaning: 工作投入感；对工作的心理参与和热情
items.definitionEn: The degree of emotional and mental involvement people have in their work.
items.usage: 本文为员工投入度，不是婚约或预约；该义通常不可数。
items.exampleEn: The survey measured engagement separately from the number of hours worked.
items.exampleZh: 问卷把工作投入感与工作时长分开测量。

items.meaning: 冷漠；缺乏兴趣和积极性
items.definitionEn: A lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.
items.usage: 通常不可数；本文讨论投入感低可能对同事造成的影响。
items.exampleEn: Managers addressed growing apathy by clarifying priorities and recognizing helpful work.
items.exampleZh: 管理者通过明确优先事项和认可助人贡献来应对日益加深的冷漠。

items.meaning: 精简流程；提高工作效率
items.definitionEn: To make a process simpler and more efficient by removing unnecessary steps.
items.usage: 强调精简与理顺流程，不必然等于削减人员。
items.exampleEn: We streamlined the approval process by removing duplicate reviews.
items.exampleZh: 我们通过取消重复审查精简了审批流程。

items.meaning: 360度反馈；来自多方关系人的综合反馈
items.definitionEn: Feedback about a person's work collected from several perspectives, such as managers, peers, and direct reports.
items.usage: 通常不是只由直属主管评分；具体反馈来源可因组织而异。
items.exampleEn: The review combined project results with 360-degree feedback from colleagues.
items.exampleZh: 这次评价结合了项目结果与来自同事的360度反馈。

items.meaning: 可用来促成改变的手段；管理杠杆
items.definitionEn: A factor or action that can be used to influence a wider outcome.
items.usage: 本文为管理比喻，指可以调整的干预手段，不是物理杠杆。
items.exampleEn: Changing approval limits was one lever for reducing unnecessary requests.
items.exampleZh: 调整审批权限上限是减少不必要请求的一项手段。

items.meaning: 负担过重的；承担过多任务的
items.definitionEn: Given more work or responsibility than can be managed comfortably or effectively.
items.usage: 本文修饰最常帮助别人的员工；不是能力弱，而可能是承担过多。
items.exampleEn: The overburdened support lead delegated routine questions to a rotating team.
items.exampleZh: 负担过重的支持负责人把常规问题交给轮值团队处理。

items.meaning: 临时的；为特定即时目的而安排的
items.definitionEn: Created or arranged for a particular immediate purpose rather than as part of a regular system.
items.usage: ad hoc 不一定表示草率或没有计划；本文用于临时发起的协作请求。
items.exampleEn: We replaced repeated ad hoc briefings with one shared weekly update.
items.exampleZh: 我们用每周一次的共享更新替代了反复进行的临时情况说明。

items.meaning: 容易遭受或出现某种不良情况的
items.definitionEn: Likely to experience something, especially an unwanted condition or problem.
items.usage: 常见 prone to + 名词或动名词，也可用 prone to do something；通常描述不良倾向或风险。
items.exampleEn: Teams with unclear priorities are more prone to repeated interruptions.
items.exampleZh: 优先事项不清晰的团队更容易受到反复打扰。

items.meaning: 遏制不断增加的事物；阻止某种趋势继续扩大
items.definitionEn: To stop or reduce a growing flow of something unwanted.
items.usage: 常接 of；本文指遏制持续涌入的请求，stem 在此为动词。
items.exampleEn: A clear help page helped stem the tide of basic account questions.
items.exampleZh: 清晰的帮助页面有助于遏制不断涌入的基础账户问题。

items.meaning: 反复发生的；定期重复的
items.definitionEn: Happening repeatedly or at regular intervals.
items.usage: 本文 recurring meetings 指日历中定期重复的会议；不一定意味着每次都有必要。
items.exampleEn: We removed a recurring meeting that no longer had a clear purpose.
items.exampleZh: 我们取消了一场已经没有明确目的的例行会议。

items.meaning: 暂停；一段中断期
items.definitionEn: A temporary break in an activity or process.
items.usage: 通常暗含之后可能恢复；不是永久取消。
items.exampleEn: The training sessions resumed after a short hiatus during the product launch.
items.exampleZh: 产品发布期间短暂停办后，培训课程恢复了。

items.meaning: 警觉的；持续留意潜在问题的
items.definitionEn: Careful and watchful in order to notice or prevent problems.
items.usage: 常接 about/against；本文强调认真审视会议安排，不是单纯勤奋。
items.exampleEn: Project leads remained vigilant about meetings that duplicated written updates.
items.exampleZh: 项目负责人持续留意那些与书面更新重复的会议。

items.meaning: 厌恶风险的；倾向于回避风险的
items.definitionEn: Preferring to avoid risk or uncertainty rather than accept possible losses.
items.usage: 本文指回避风险的组织文化可能促使成员过度请求审批。
items.exampleEn: A risk-averse approval culture made staff seek permission for minor purchases.
items.exampleZh: 回避风险的审批文化让员工连小额采购都要请示。

items.meaning: 利益相关者；受决策影响或能影响决策的一方
items.definitionEn: A person or group with an interest in, influence over, or exposure to the effects of an activity.
items.usage: stakeholder 范围比 shareholder 股东更广，可包括客户、员工和合作方。
items.exampleEn: We consulted key stakeholders before changing the service schedule.
items.exampleZh: 在调整服务时间表之前，我们咨询了主要利益相关方。

items.meaning: 有效利用某种资源以取得更大效果
items.definitionEn: To use an available resource or advantage to achieve a useful result.
items.usage: 本文为动词，指利用技术与空间；不是财务杠杆的名词义。
items.exampleEn: We leveraged the existing forum to answer questions across all regional teams.
items.exampleZh: 我们利用现有论坛回答所有区域团队的问题。

items.meaning: 有害的；造成不利影响的
items.definitionEn: Causing harm or making a situation worse.
items.usage: 常用 detrimental to something；effects 为被修饰名词时也常见。
items.exampleEn: Frequent context switching can be detrimental to careful analytical work.
items.exampleZh: 频繁切换任务可能不利于需要细致思考的分析工作。

items.meaning: 将需要协作的人员安排在同一地点
items.definitionEn: To place people or activities together in the same physical location.
items.usage: 原文采用 colocate 拼写，也可见 co-locate；不是要求所有工作一律回到办公室。
items.exampleEn: We colocated the testing and support teams during the two-week pilot.
items.exampleZh: 在为期两周的试点期间，我们把测试和支持团队安排在同一地点。

items.meaning: 相互依赖的；彼此需要配合才能完成工作的
items.definitionEn: Depending on one another so that each person's or part's work affects the others.
items.usage: 强调双向或多方依赖；不是单纯存在联系。
items.exampleEn: The two interdependent teams agreed on a shared handover checklist.
items.exampleZh: 这两个相互依赖的团队约定使用一份共同的交接清单。

items.meaning: 促进；使某个过程更容易开展
items.definitionEn: To make an activity or process easier to carry out.
items.usage: 不等于亲自替所有人完成任务；可通过安排环境、资源或流程来促进。
items.exampleEn: A shared vocabulary facilitated communication between finance and engineering.
items.exampleZh: 共同的术语体系促进了财务与工程部门之间的沟通。

items.meaning: 即兴的；事先未安排的
items.definitionEn: Happening without advance planning or preparation.
items.usage: 本文指简短的临时面对面合作；不等于低质量或没有价值。
items.exampleEn: An impromptu conversation solved the issue before a formal meeting was needed.
items.exampleZh: 一次临时交谈在需要正式开会之前就解决了问题。

items.meaning: 决策权；就特定事项作出决定的权限
items.definitionEn: The authority assigned to a person or group to make particular decisions.
items.usage: 强调哪些决定由谁作出；不同于只提供建议或最后执行。
items.exampleEn: The project charter clarified decision rights for changes to customer requirements.
items.exampleZh: 项目章程明确了变更客户需求的决策权限。

items.meaning: 资本性支出；用于购置或改善长期资产的支出
items.definitionEn: Money spent to acquire or improve assets expected to be used over a longer period.
items.usage: 常见缩写 CapEx；与日常运营支出不同，本文讨论这类支出的审批权限。
items.exampleEn: The equipment upgrade required approval as a capital expenditure.
items.exampleZh: 这项设备升级需要作为资本性支出获得批准。

items.meaning: 缓冲机制；减少直接冲击或需求压力的中间安排
items.definitionEn: Something that absorbs pressure or reduces the direct effect of demands on a person or system.
items.usage: 本文指有人或机制先接住求助需求，保护最繁忙员工的时间。
items.exampleEn: A rotating help desk created a buffer between routine questions and specialist work.
items.exampleZh: 轮值服务台在常规问题与专家工作之间形成了缓冲。

items.meaning: 多面手；能够承担多种支持任务的人员
items.definitionEn: A versatile person who can fill different roles or respond to varied needs.
items.usage: 原为体育用语；本文比喻可轮值处理不同求助任务的人员。
items.exampleEn: Each week, a utility player handled small requests that would otherwise interrupt specialists.
items.exampleZh: 每周由一位多面手处理原本会打扰专家的小请求。

items.meaning: 认为；认定
items.definitionEn: To judge or consider someone or something to have a particular quality or status.
items.usage: 较正式；常用 deem someone something 或 be deemed to be。
items.exampleEn: Only proposals deemed feasible by the review team moved to testing.
items.exampleZh: 只有被审查团队认定为可行的提案才进入测试阶段。

items.meaning: 表现不及预期；未达到应有水平
items.definitionEn: To perform less well than expected or required.
items.usage: 可用于个人、团队或项目；本文强调表现低可能与过载有关，而非缺乏能力。
items.exampleEn: A talented employee may underperform when constant interruptions fragment the day.
items.exampleZh: 当持续打扰把一天切得支离破碎时，有才干的员工也可能表现不及预期。

items.meaning: 赞誉；认可
items.definitionEn: Praise or recognition given for an achievement.
items.usage: 通常不可数，虽以 s 结尾也不机械理解为复数；常用 earn/get kudos。
items.exampleEn: The coordinator earned kudos for helping three teams meet the deadline.
items.exampleZh: 这位协调员因帮助三个团队按时完成任务而获得赞誉。

items.meaning: 扩大；增强某种效果或他人的成功
items.definitionEn: To increase the strength, extent, or effect of something.
items.usage: 本文为比喻义，指帮助放大同事的成果；不只是扩音设备用语。
items.exampleEn: Sharing the reusable tool amplified the impact of one analyst's work.
items.exampleZh: 分享这套可复用工具放大了一位分析师工作的影响。

items.meaning: 绩效指标；用于衡量表现的量化标准
items.definitionEn: A measure used to evaluate how well a person, team, or process performs.
items.usage: 指标应与真实目标一致；本文提醒同时衡量个人成果与协作贡献。
items.exampleEn: We added a performance metric for the quality of cross-team handovers.
items.exampleZh: 我们新增了一项衡量跨团队交接质量的绩效指标。

items.meaning: 收购；一家公司购买另一家公司或其业务
items.definitionEn: A transaction in which one company buys another company or part of its business.
items.usage: 本文为企业并购义；不是知识或技能的习得。
items.exampleEn: During the acquisition, management mapped which employees held critical relationships.
items.exampleZh: 收购期间，管理层梳理了哪些员工掌握着关键关系。

items.meaning: 整合；把分散设施或业务合并集中
items.definitionEn: To combine separate operations or facilities into a more unified arrangement.
items.usage: 本文指整合世界各地设施；不直接等于裁员，尽管重组可能伴随人员变化。
items.exampleEn: The firm consolidated its regional support centers into two shared hubs.
items.exampleZh: 公司把区域支持中心整合为两个共享枢纽。

items.meaning: 留任奖金；鼓励员工继续留职的奖励
items.definitionEn: An additional payment offered to encourage an employee to remain with an organization.
items.usage: 重点是留住员工，不是新员工签约奖金；是否留任仍取决于具体条件。
items.exampleEn: The retention bonus recognized specialists whose knowledge was essential during the transition.
items.exampleZh: 留任奖金认可了那些在过渡期拥有关键知识的专家。

items.meaning: 准确找出；精确识别
items.definitionEn: To identify the exact location, source, or nature of something.
items.usage: 强调准确定位，而不只是笼统知道存在问题或重要人员。
items.exampleEn: Network data helped us pinpoint who was receiving repeated requests.
items.exampleZh: 网络数据帮助我们准确找出了哪些人反复收到求助请求。

items.meaning: 先决条件；必须事先满足的要求
items.definitionEn: A condition that must be met before something else can happen.
items.usage: 常用 a prerequisite for/to；本文指有效共享资源应成为正面评价与晋升的条件。
items.exampleEn: Reliable documentation became a prerequisite for handing the service to another team.
items.exampleZh: 可靠的文档成了把这项服务交接给另一团队的先决条件。

items.meaning: 交叉销售；向已有客户销售相关的其他产品或服务
items.definitionEn: To offer an existing customer additional related products or services.
items.usage: 不同于 upsell 推销更贵或更高阶版本；本文涉及不同业务间合作创造客户价值。
items.exampleEn: The account teams worked together to cross-sell a reporting service to existing clients.
items.exampleZh: 客户团队协作向现有客户交叉销售一项报告服务。

items.meaning: 标准；用于判断或筛选的依据
items.definitionEn: A standard used to make a judgment or decide whether something qualifies.
items.usage: 单数 criterion，复数 criteria；不要把 criteria 当作单数。
items.exampleEn: One criterion for the award was the ability to help other teams succeed.
items.exampleZh: 该奖项的一项评选标准是帮助其他团队成功的能力。

items.meaning: 在不同要求之间取得合理平衡
items.definitionEn: To achieve an appropriate balance between competing needs or priorities.
items.usage: 常用 strike a balance between A and B；healthy 表示合理、可持续。
items.exampleEn: We tried to strike a healthy balance between deep work and helping colleagues.
items.exampleZh: 我们努力在专注工作与帮助同事之间取得合理平衡。

items.meaning: 紧迫的；需要立即关注的
items.definitionEn: Urgent and requiring prompt attention.
items.usage: 本文为紧迫义，不是压、按；不表示每个请求都应被标为紧急。
items.exampleEn: The team postponed minor updates to address a pressing customer issue.
items.exampleZh: 团队推迟了小更新，以处理一个紧迫的客户问题。

items.meaning: 承担代价；承受负面后果
items.definitionEn: To experience or accept the financial, practical, or personal consequences of something.
items.usage: costs 在此不仅是金钱，也包括时间、精力及工作受损的代价。
items.exampleEn: Junior staff should not bear the costs of unclear management priorities.
items.exampleZh: 初级员工不应承担管理层优先事项不清的代价。

items.meaning: 最大的一份；绝大部分
items.definitionEn: The largest share of something, especially work, responsibility, or benefits.
items.usage: 本文用于侧栏讨论女性承担较多协作工作；不是固定指超过某个精确百分比。
items.exampleEn: One coordinator handled the lion's share of the event preparations.
items.exampleZh: 一位协调员承担了活动准备工作中的绝大部分。
collocations: the lion's share of the work
